chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fudayl, who said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah informed us, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Nahik al-Samuri narrated to me from Ubays ibn Hisham al-Nashiri from Salih ibn Sa'id al-Qammam from Yunus ibn Abi Yahya, who said:

I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he arrived in al-Hirah, and he mentioned a hadith that he narrated to us, except that he said he traveled with him until he reached the place he intended. He said, 'O Yunus, tie your mount.' So I tied them together. Then he raised his hand and made a quiet supplication that I did not understand. Then he began the prayer and recited two short surahs, pronouncing them audibly, and I did as he did. Then he made supplication (peace be upon him), and I understood and knew it. He said, 'O Yunus, do you know what place this is?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, by Allah, but I know that I am in the desert.' He said, 'This is the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); he and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will meet on the Day of Resurrection.'

The supplication: 'O Allah, there is no avoiding Your command, no avoiding Your decree, no avoiding Your judgment, and no power and no strength except with You. O Allah, then whatever judgment You have judged for us or whatever decree You have decreed for us, grant us with it a patience that overcomes it and repels it, and make it rising in Your pleasure, increasing in our good deeds, our excellence, our stability, our honor, our glory, our blessings, and our dignity in this world and the hereafter.'

And whatever gift You have given us, or with which You have favored us from a virtue, or with which You have honored us from a dignity, grant us with it a gratitude that overcomes it and repels it, and make it rising in Your pleasure, in our good deeds, our stability, our honor, Your blessings, and Your dignity in this world and the hereafter. And do not make it for us arrogance or extravagance, or a trial, or hatred, or punishment, or disgrace in this world or in the hereafter.

O Allah, we seek refuge in You from the stumble of the tongue, and the evil of the station, and the lightness of the scale. O Allah, present our good deeds to us at death, and do not show us our actions upon us as regrets, and do not disgrace us at Your judgment, and do not expose us with our bad deeds on the day we meet You. And make our hearts remember You and not forget You, and fear You as if they see You when they meet You. And turn our bad deeds into good deeds, and make our good deeds ranks, and make our ranks chambers, and make our chambers high.

O Allah, and expand for our poor from Your vastness what You decreed upon Yourself, and guidance as long as You keep us alive, and dignity as long as You keep us alive, and dignity when You take our souls, and protection in what remains of our lifespan, and blessing in what You have provided for us, and help with what You have burdened us with, and steadfastness with what You have encircled us with. And do not hold us accountable for our injustice, and do not punish us for our ignorance, and do not entice us with our mistakes. And make the best of what we say established in our hearts.

And make us great in Your sight, humble in ourselves, and benefit us with what You have taught us, and increase us in beneficial knowledge. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a heart that does not humble itself, an eye that does not weep, and a prayer that is not accepted. Deliver us from the evil of trials, O Guardian of this world and the hereafter.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.خِفَّةُ الْمِيزَان: Lightness of the scale (on Judgment Day)
key_terms.عَثْرَةُ اللِّسَان: Stumble of the tongue (speaking unintentionally or foolishly)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by Imam al-Sadiq at the grave of Ali ibn Abi Talib in al-Hirah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia tradition of identifying al-Hirah as the burial site of Imam Ali, emphasizing the spiritual merit of praying and supplicating at his grave. The Imam’s detailed dua reflects core Shia theological themes, including acceptance of divine decree (*al-qada' wa al-qadar*), the transformation of sins into good deeds, and the balance between humility and dignity in the presence of God.
